newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian broker upgrades Bekaert rating.
newsitem.headline: Belgian broker upgrades Bekaert rating.

text.p: Belgian brokerage KB-Securities said on Friday it raised its rating for shares in Belgian steel cord and wire maker Bekaert.

"We have upgraded our investment recommendation from Hold+ to Buy", said analyst Pascale Weber. This is based on a current price level of 18,150 francs which implied a price/earnings ratio (P/E) of 16.6 for 1997 and 14.2 for 1998.
On the Brussels bourse Bekaert stock was up 3.5 percent at 19,200 francs at 1335 GMT after having suffered heavy losses this week in the wake of a company warning on 1996 profit.

"Current net profits are expected to fall from 3.2 billion francs in 1995 to break-even in 1996. Fifty percent of this fall is the result of lower activity, especially in the steel cord sector," she said.
But the stock offered an attractive gross dividend yield of 3.3 percent based on a maintained dividend for 1996. It paid 600 francs in 1995.
"We continue to believe in Bekaert's focused management and the group's expansion potential outside Western Europe."
She added that an announced restructuring programme would bolster results from 1997 because of lower employee costs and higher capacity utilisation.
